stem:
Qadir has two triangles. Each angle of the first equals the matching angle of the second, but one triangle has sides twice as long as the other.

Are the triangles congruent?

options.text: Yes: they are the same shape, and same shape means congruent.
Yes: the matching equal angles alone settle congruence.
No: equal angles give the same shape, but different sizes mean the triangles need not be congruent.
Yes, because the printed word twice is the standout cue in the stem.

teacher.key_rationale: AAA gives similarity of shape, not congruence of size. Relabeling as same shape, dropping the size difference, or grabbing the printed word twice all miss that equal angles alone do not force congruence.
